Independent review of run r-20260921T102128084713-fleet-drain-guard-fires-on-this-cluster, plan imas-ambix:slurm-hosted-agent-fleet section 7 (the drain warning on the fleet's allocation node state). Read at 555be4ac00dcd77a7c3460e5f6eadf696dcd7e88 on base 8223d94d373ae3738e4abc7595ac2a1c6f1c719a. The two commits are unmerged and sit in the reviewed run's own worktree; every measurement below was taken from the reviewed blobs, never from the merged head, and the reviewer wrote nothing inside the reviewed worktree.

VERDICT goal: the goal is to attach an independent review of whether the drain guard now fires on the commits that were written to repair it. It does. Measured over a census this reviewer took (428 live nodes, ten distinct State values, 82 carrying a drain token) the reviewed predicate fires on all 82 draining nodes and on none of the 346 that carry no drain token, where the pre-fix revision fires on 0 of the 82 from the same census with the same harness.

VERDICT done_when: the four questions the evidence fence names are answered below with a verdict and the returned measurement for each; the record is a parsed JSON object scoring five dimensions inside 0..20; and the covered change is correct in both directions.

VERDICT write_paths: the reviewed diff 8223d94d..555be4ac touches exactly the five paths its manifest declares -- imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py, tests/agent/test_fleet.py, docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html (three lines), docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html and docs/figures/fleet-drain-guard/drain-token-position.svg (2761 bytes, present). imas_ambix/agent/cli.py carries no diff, which is the right call: the drain predicate is reached through describe_fleet_allocation and the two guard branches were covered from tests alone.

VERDICT manifest: cross-checked against the artifacts rather than read for plausibility. The census it quotes re-derives exactly from its own log: 510 rows, 180 ALLOCATED, 115 IDLE, 82 RESUME, 43 MIXED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED, 42 MIXED, 39 ALLOCATED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED, 5 DOWN, 1 MIXED+RESERVED, 1 IDLE+MAINTENANCE+RESERVED, 1 DOWN+NOT_RESPONDING, 1 ALLOCATED+MAINTENANCE+RESERVED -- so 82 drain-carrying nodes and zero leading with the token, as recorded. The declared mutation file is a single line and the receipt's first line is byte-identical to it, so the verbatim rule covers the whole declaration rather than part of it. The gate summaries match what this reviewer measured at the same revision (20 passed; ruff exit 0 read from the run's log).

VERDICT diff: read commit by commit. 45f4cd8d drops the leading-token truncation in parse_node_state and replaces the leading-token prefix match in node_is_draining with a per-token sweep, with docstrings that state why the leading token is not privileged; it adds five tests covering the drain direction (both real spellings), the false-positive direction (four healthy forms, one of them flag-carrying), the two unknown-state branches, and a predicate table over the real spellings in both directions, and replaces one test that asserted the truncated form. 555be4ac corrects the landed record where it had stated the flag direction as fact and adds the evidence anchor, the figure and the plan comment. Both commits carry conventional subjects with real bodies and no trailer.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 18
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the repair does what the goal states, and it is the exact clause the previous review of this thread failed on (that review scored it 13 because the predicate fired on 0 of the 82 draining nodes this cluster reports). Measured here over a census taken at review time: the reviewed predicate fires on 82 of 82 drain-carrying nodes, and the pre-fix revision on the same census fires on 0 of 82, parsing MIXED and ALLOCATED respectively -- so the fix is load-bearing rather than incidental. Docked two because the deliverable's own proof never touched a live node state: the firing certificate is a faked runner's node_state string, and the guard exists precisely for the live spelling, which one `scontrol show node <name>` answers at zero cost. The node disclosed this in the record and this review closed it by observation, but the record as delivered still certifies its central claim with fixtures.

SCORE evidence: 15
JUSTIFICATION evidence: the receipts taken are real and were re-derived instead of trusted. The census log re-derivation is exact to the node counts above, which is the strongest available check that the record's numbers are the instrument's and not a summary of them. The declared mutation's first line is byte-identical to the declared text and the declared file is a single line, so the verbatim rule covers the whole declaration rather than part of it. The receipt shows the red at the named test id under the mutation (MUTATED_EXIT=1) and the green after restore (GREEN_EXIT=0). Docked because (i) the firing proof is fixture-bound, so the population that could have falsified it was never read; (ii) the restore step inside the receipt is a self-assertion -- the log line says the file was verified identical to the backup, but the receipt shows no comparison output, so the restoration is certified by the receipt's own claim about itself rather than by a shown result (this reviewer confirmed it independently from the committed source, which carries the sweep, so the artifact is right even though that particular receipt is weak); and (iii) the sections of the record are strong on what was measured and silent on the one live reading that was available.

SCORE durability: 17
JUSTIFICATION durability: the property the previous review docked hardest is exactly what now holds. The undeclared-premise fixture is gone: both real spellings are asserted as data. After a mutation restoring the leading-token behaviour, the named test is observed to fail, so a regression to the predicate that could not fire is caught by the suite rather than by a reader. Both directions are covered as data, including a flag-carrying healthy form (MIXED+RESERVED) and the two unknown-state branches, which were previously inspection. Docked three because the suite's drain coverage away from the wins is thinner than the record implies: the CLI-level healthy case asserts the state stays silent only incidental to the row being unbounded, the assertion that a query was not issued is expressed as an argument-count proxy rather than by naming the subcommand, and the receipt's restore is self-asserted as recorded above.

SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: the change follows the grammar of the value it reads, which is the ground the previous review's fit dock rested on. A scheduler State= is a `+`-separated token set, so returning the whole upper-cased value and sweeping every token is the shape the data has; the docstrings state the mechanism (the drain token is not necessarily first, and this cluster reports it second) rather than narrating the edit, the constant keeps its existing name and gains a corrected comment, and the warning appends in the module's existing describe_* idiom. The landed record was corrected in place where it had generalised from its own fixture -- the scrub-as-you-pass rule applied to documentation rather than left standing. Docked two for the one consumer delta the record does not mention anywhere: the warning sentence now quotes the whole state value rather than the leading token.

SCORE scope_discipline: 19
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: the diff lands in exactly the declared paths and nowhere else, cli.py is untouched, both commits are conventional with real bodies and no AI attribution (line-anchored check on both), and the naming sweeps over the 142 added source lines return no plan label, ticket reference, version suffix or author attribution, as does the path sweep. Docked one for the fence overlap the node disclosed: its declared write paths intersect those of a concurrently fenced node on imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py and tests/agent/test_fleet.py. The overlap was not contended (the peer's work had already landed at 5b6f84e7 before this node ran, and the manifest says so transparently), but the overlap itself is the thing the fence exists to prevent and a reader should not have to reconstruct that it was benign.

FINDING docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html (the section 'What this record does not establish'): the guard's firing is certified by a faked runner's node_state string and by the mutation-forced red, never by a live node state, so the record's central claim rests on a fixture written from the same census.

The node declares this as a follow-on and the record states it plainly, which is the honest half; the gap is that the falsifying population was one read away. Closed by this review: the production command `scontrol show node` run against three live draining nodes (98dci4-clu-3025, -3032, -3052, each reported ALLOCATED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED) through the reviewed module yields the warning line for each, so the guard's firing is now observed against an observed drain rather than a faked state.

FINDING negative-control.log: the restoration is self-asserted. The line '--- RESTORE: fleet.py restored from backup, verified identical ---' claims a comparison the receipt does not show, so a restart-from-mutation failure and a clean restore are indistinguishable from the log alone; the green re-run after it is the real evidence that the restore took. Confirmed independently here -- the committed blob carries the token sweep ('for token in state.upper().split("+")' present in the head, and 'split("+", 1)' absent from parse_node_state) -- so the artifact is correct and the finding is about the receipt's strength, not the tree's state.

FINDING tests/agent/test_fleet.py (test_fleet_status_reads_a_non_node_value_as_unknown): the negative half of that assertion is expressed as `not any(command[0] == "scontrol" and len(command) > 3 for command in commands)`, an argument-count proxy for 'the node query was not issued'. It is non-vacuous here -- the sibling test over the same recorder asserts `any(...)` with the same predicate, so the instrument is shown able to see a query -- but naming the subcommand instead of counting arguments would say what is meant at the same cost and would not admit a differently-argumented scontrol call.

ANSWER (a) whether the guard now fires on EVERY drain spelling the live node table actually contains, checked against a census taken by this reviewer: YES. Census taken at review time with `scontrol show node -o` (the same command the code's own path reaches): 428 nodes, ten distinct State values. 82 of them carry a drain token -- 43 at MIXED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED and 39 at ALLOCATED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED, and none of the 82 leads with it. The reviewed predicate fires on all 82 and misses none; the pre-fix revision, exercised through the identical harness over the identical census, fires on 0 of 82 with parsed=MIXED and parsed=ALLOCATED. Off-census spellings behave correctly too (DRAIN, DRAINED, DRAINING and ALLOCATED+DRAIN all fire). Live end-to-end: the production `scontrol show node <name>` for three real draining nodes, fed to the production key, fires with the operator-facing warning line. And the real CLI (`agent fleet status`, with the serving tree confirmed by printing the module's own __file__) reads the live allocation 1274732 on 98dci4-clu-2002 and correctly prints no warning, because that node is not draining -- so the pass is a property of the state, not of the command. Note the census has moved since the run's reading (the run recorded 82 RESUME nodes, gone now; 510 nodes then, 428 now), and the two readings agree on what matters: 82 drain-carrying nodes, zero leading with the token.

ANSWER (b) whether it can raise a FALSE warning on any non-draining state present in that same census: NO. The 346 nodes carrying no drain token are silent under the reviewed predicate, across every non-draining spelling the census contains (ALLOCATED, IDLE, MIXED, DOWN, DOWN+NOT_RESPONDING, MIXED+RESERVED, IDLE+MAINTENANCE+RESERVED, ALLOCATED+MAINTENANCE+RESERVED).

The false-positive probe that matters most is off-census: UNDRAIN, the scheduler's token for a node returned to service, does not start with DRAIN, so the sweep stays silent -- a naive substring match on 'DRAIN' would have come on in the un-drain case and this does not.

ANSWER (c) whether the parser change altered behaviour for any other caller of parse_node_state: NO other caller exists, and the one delta the sole caller sees is the fix itself. Enumerated tree-wide over the reviewed revision: the only production caller is `_fleet_node_state` in imas_ambix/agent/cli.py (lines 1260-1273, unchanged by this run), whose sole consumer is describe_fleet_allocation at cli.py:343-344; node_is_draining's only other use is fleet.py:207 inside that same function; nothing else in the tree references either symbol outside the tests. The delta the caller sees is two-fold: the drain predicate now sees the drain token inside the set (the intended repair), and the warning sentence now quotes the whole state value where it previously quoted the leading token ('the scheduler reports MIXED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED' rather than '...reports MIXED'). Nothing compares the returned value for equality to a token and no other consumer parses that string, so no unintended behaviour change exists anywhere. The one behaviour change outside the predicate is the quoted value in that one sentence, which is a gain for the operator and is stated here because no record in the tree mentions it.

ANSWER (d) whether the run self-reported honestly: YES, on both statements, and the second is conservative rather than generous. (1) Of the two self-introduced failures it declares: the replaced test asserted the truncated form as the contract -- `assert parse_node_state("   State=DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING\n") == "DRAINING"` is removed by the diff, and the run's own stream records that exact failure (assert 'DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING' == 'DRAINING') before the two replacement tests were written; the lint break is likewise in the stream against the exact assertion line (`assert not any(command[0] == "scontrol" and len(command) < 3 ...)`), and the fix is visible in the committed form, where that line is wrapped across three lines -- a marker the head still carries, which is stronger than the transcript alone.

Neither claim is inflated and no third self-introduced failure is visible in the range. (2) The declared follow-on that the guard is proven by a faked state rather than by an observed drain is accurate: the record's own 'What this record does not establish' says so, the tests confirm it (the faked runner is the only node-state source in the suite), and nothing in the delivered evidence observes a live drain. The statement is therefore a true limitation disclosed by the run, and this review has since produced the missing observation, which makes the run's sentence conservative rather than generous.

Note for the next reader: what remains is not a defect but an unexplained delta -- the warning sentence now quotes the whole State value instead of the leading token, which is an operator-visible improvement and is unmentioned in the record -- and the fixture-bound certificate, which this review closed by running the production key against live draining nodes rather than by re-reading the fixtures. Nothing here was judged against the merged head; a separately dispatched test node owns that.

The reviewer wrote nothing inside the reviewed worktree or the repository; the probe scripts and logs named in its manifest are the artifacts of run r-20260921T112040057689-review-of-drain-guard.
